Summary: Cart is unusable for problem_user: items are not added and the cart page never opens
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Log in as problem_user 2) Click Add to cart on the first product 3) Click Add to cart on the second product 4) Click the cart icon
Expected Result: Badge shows 2 and the cart page lists both items
Actual Result: No badge appears after either click, the cart icon does not navigate and the URL stays /inventory.html
Evidence: Verified with the Selenium probe, reproduced in 3 runs

Summary: All six product tiles show the same image for problem_user
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Open the inventory page 2) Compare the src attribute of the six product images
Expected Result: Each product shows its own image
Actual Result: All six img elements share one src (1 unique src for 6 products)
Evidence: Verified with the Selenium probe (DOM inspection)

Summary: Sorting has no effect for problem_user
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Select Price (high to low) in the sort dropdown 2) Read the product prices
Expected Result: Prices are sorted descending

Summary: Cart contents survive logout and are visible to a different account
Preconditions: standard_user has one product in the cart
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Add Sauce Labs Backpack as standard_user 2) Log out 3) Log in as problem_user 4) Inspect the inventory buttons and the cart
Expected Result: A new session starts with an empty cart
Actual Result: Backpack still shows a Remove button and the badge shows 1 after logging in as problem_user

Summary: performance_glitch_user inventory renders about 80x slower than standard_user
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Log in as performance_glitch_user and time the moment the six product cards render 2) Repeat with standard_user
Expected Result: All demo accounts render the inventory in comparable time
Actual Result: 5459 ms for performance_glitch_user against 69 ms for standard_user on the same page
Evidence: Timed with WebDriverWait in the Selenium probe

Summary: Checkout can be started with an empty cart
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Log in as standard_user 2) Open the cart 3) Click Checkout
Expected Result: Checkout is blocked until the cart contains at least one item
Actual Result: The Checkout button is enabled and /checkout-step-one.html opens with an empty order

Summary: Checkout accepts a whitespace-only first name
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Open checkout step one 2) Enter three spaces in First Name 3) Fill Last Name and Postal Code 4) Click Continue
Expected Result: A required-field error is shown for the first name
Actual Result: The value is accepted and the order overview opens

Summary: Checkout accepts a non-numeric postal code
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Open checkout step one 2) Enter ABCDE in Postal Code 3) Click Continue
Expected Result: The postal code format is validated before continuing
Actual Result: The order overview opens

Summary: Login fields define no maximum length
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Inspect the maxlength attribute of the username and password fields
Expected Result: Both fields define a maximum input length
Actual Result: Neither field has a maxlength attribute
Evidence: Verified with the Selenium probe (DOM inspection)

Summary: Sort preference resets after leaving the inventory page
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Sort by Price (high to low) 2) Open the cart 3) Return to the inventory
Expected Result: The previously selected sort is kept
Actual Result: The dropdown falls back to Name (A to Z)

Summary: Login inputs are not programmatically associated with the error banner
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Submit wrong credentials 2) Inspect the username and password inputs
Expected Result: Both inputs reference the error message via aria-describedby
Actual Result: The error has role=alert but neither input has aria-describedby
Evidence: Verified with the Selenium probe (DOM inspection)

Summary: No password recovery path on the login page
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Look for a forgot password link or recovery flow
Expected Result: Users can recover access to their account
Actual Result: No recovery link or flow exists

Summary: Password cannot be revealed while typing
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Type a password 2) Look for a show/hide control
Expected Result: An optional reveal control is available
Actual Result: No toggle exists; the field is always masked

Summary: Cart offers no quantity control, so the same product cannot be bought twice
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Open the cart 2) Look for a quantity field 3) Return to the inventory and add the same product again
Expected Result: Quantity can be changed and the same product can be added twice
Actual Result: The cart has no quantity input and a second add does not change the quantity

Summary: Inventory has no product search or filter
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Look for a search box on the inventory page
Expected Result: Users can search the catalogue
Actual Result: No search input or filter exists

Summary: Inventory list has no pagination
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Scroll through the inventory list
Expected Result: Large catalogues are paginated
Actual Result: All products render on a single page with no pagination controls

Summary: Order confirmation page shows no order number
Preconditions: An order has just been completed
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Complete an order 2) Read the confirmation page
Expected Result: The confirmation shows an order reference the customer can quote
Actual Result: The page text contains no order number or identifier

Summary: Customer has no order history
Preconditions: An order has just been completed
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Look for an account or orders area
Expected Result: Previous orders can be reviewed
Actual Result: No order history or account section exists

Summary: Order overview offers no way to edit the cart
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Look for an edit action next to the items
Expected Result: Items can be changed before the order is finished
Actual Result: Only Cancel is available

Summary: Products never show availability information
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Inspect the product tiles for any stock or availability state
Expected Result: Availability is shown for each product
Actual Result: No stock or availability text exists on the page

Summary: Checkout overview is reachable with an empty cart and renders a $0.00 order
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Log in as standard_user 2) Open /checkout-step-two.html directly
Expected Result: The user is redirected to the cart
Actual Result: The overview renders with Total: $0.00 and an active Finish button
